title: Measuring DD in headless Claude Code sessions: warm the resident and read the report before the Stop hook
body:
Do not set DD_RESIDENT=0 in the agent's environment; give each run its own DD_RESIDENT_REGISTRY, start its resident, and probe readiness by piping a session-start payload into hooks/run.cjs until the output has additionalContext without 'DD - Inactive'. Register hooks from the plugin's hooks/hooks.json, not by hand. Read the agent's task report from the stream-json events (--verbose --include-hook-events): the assistant text after its last tool call and before the Stop hook_response that adds context; the result event's text is the reply to DD's Stop-hook capture reminder. Treat the 20 ms timing test in tests/hooks/resident.test.js as flaky in fresh clones when using the suite as a regression signal.

Why: In the 2026-10-07 smoke run the agent's SessionStart said 'DD - Inactive: ... DD_RESIDENT=0' while prompt and pre-tool hooks still delivered memories, so the September trial likely measured DD without its session start. With DD hooks the final result was "I'm not proposing a memory from this turn", which a blind judge read as the task report, penalizing DD and revealing it. The resident timing test failed in four fresh clones across both conditions and passed 3/3 once warm.

evidence.summary: startResident warm-up via session-start hook, per-run DD_RESIDENT_REGISTRY, ddSettings from hooks/hooks.json, KNOWN_FLAKY, taskReport used for check and judge
taskReport stops at a Stop hook_response that adds context; tested in tests/engine/cognition/agent-metrics.test.js
residentNotice returns 'DD - Inactive: the resident DD process is disabled (DD_RESIDENT=0)' for state disabled
the first-prompt test waits setTimeout 20 ms for the model-loaded transition

v1.trigger: When running Claude Code headless with DD's hooks to measure or evaluate DD, in src/eval/agent/run.js or any new harness or benchmark
